title: MR cholangiography (MRCP)
what: An MRI of the belly that shows the bile ducts, gallbladder and the pancreatic duct. No needle and no radiation.
why: When gallstones in the bile ducts are suspected, for jaundice, for pain under the right ribs and before surgery.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes, the report in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you have a pacemaker, metal implants or metal fragments
If you are afraid of closed spaces
If you have kidney disease - if contrast is planned

prepare.title: Fasting
prepare.text: Usually no food or drink for 4 to 6 hours, so the gallbladder is full. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off jewelry, watch and belt. Leave cards and phone in the locker.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Your usual medicines can usually be taken with a small sip of water. Ask your doctor.

bring: Blood test results, if you had them
steps: You change clothes and remove all metal
You lie on your back on the scanner table
A coil - a light pad - is placed on your belly
The table slides into the scanner and you are given earphones
You are often asked to hold your breath on command
Sometimes contrast is given into a vein
feel: The scanner knocks loudly - this is normal
Breath holds are tiring, but short
after: You can eat and go about your day right away
The report is usually ready in 1 to 3 days
Discuss the result with your doctor

faq.a: Often the ducts can be seen without it. The doctor decides.
So the gallbladder and ducts are full, and the bowel gets in the way less.

reminders.text: MRI of the bile ducts tomorrow. Do not eat for 4 to 6 hours before. Take off all metal.
